# Methodological Assessment

This folder contains evaluations of the methodological validity and practical utility of clinical scoring systems used for risk adjustment in healthcare auditing. It highlights the persistent tension between comprehensive data collection and routine clinical feasibility, specifically critiquing tools like P-POSSUM, APACHE, and the Surgical Apgar Score in the context of quality indicators such as Indikator 5. Ultimately, the analysis underscores the ongoing challenge of identifying risk stratification methods that are both pragmatically viable for clinical staff and inclusive of all relevant patient risk profiles.

## Pages

- [[methodological-assessment|Methodological Assessment]] — Evaluates the practical and physiological limitations of clinical scoring systems like P-POSSUM, APACHE, and the Surgical Apgar Score when applied to specific quality indicators.
